battle.name: 波斯第一次入侵希臘
battle.brief: 公元前492年，波斯王大流士一世渡過赫勒斯滂海峽，取色雷斯與馬其頓，再於前490年進軍阿提卡。卡面的亞述長弓是公元前七世紀亞述弓兵用的短型複合反曲弓，波斯弓兵承襲其射術體系；馬拉松一役，波斯以弓矢與車兵布陣，卻在希臘方陣的包抄下折翼退去。

kit.name: 亞述長弓
kit.history: 亞述人靠弓和鐵的組合征服兩河流域。弓兵在車上射，車兵靠弓兵開路。

countries: 公元前492年開始的波斯第一次入侵希臘，是阿契美尼德帝國第一次以舉國之力向歐洲方向發動的戰役，交戰雙方是波斯帝國與希臘城邦聯盟。波斯方的編制並非單一民族軍隊，而是以波斯人與米底人為核心的帝國徵召體系：大流士一世自稱萬王之王，在薩迪斯與波斯波利斯設有總督（薩特拉普），各行省按人口、兵役與物資分攤名額。遠征軍由國王親領，分為主軍與分遣縱隊；主軍在安納索斯山口被色雷斯的騎兵襲擊後，仍以步兵方陣與弓兵縱隊穩步南進，另一支分遣隊則被派往多瑙河方向，企圖牽制北方。軍中核心是亞述—米底—波斯一脈相承的複合弓步兵：弓兵自攜箭袋，大批雇傭的投石手與輕裝矛兵配置在兩翼，另有波斯重裝步兵與車兵。右翼與前鋒由伊奧尼亞人、呂底亞人、卡里亞人、佛里吉亞人、薩卡人、薩爾馬提亞人與埃及人湊成的混合部隊組成，車隊由波斯貴族與薩卡人駕御，另有象隊參與。艦隊則由腓尼基人、塞浦路斯人、塞浦利科亞人、埃及人與仍效忠波斯的伊奧尼亞人拼成，配備撞角與登城塔，負責攻擊埃雷特里亞並掩護登陸。希臘方的編制以城邦為單位：雅典的十將軍委員會由民選產生，每人一票，出兵與否由五百人議會及公民大會決定，執政官會議（阿瑞奧帕古斯）居於其上；埃雷特里亞是優布亞島上的小城邦；普拉提亞雖小卻是最早站出來的盟友；色雷斯的聯邦騎兵在安納索斯山口一度得手；斯巴達與雅典聯手馳援色雷斯，卻在半途因傳聞波斯人要攻擊伯羅奔尼撒而折返，色雷斯人因此對聯盟心生怨懟。整體而言，波斯以百萬量級的總兵力與數百艘戰艦對上分散而缺乏統一指揮的城邦聯盟，這正是這場戰爭在體量與性質上的根本落差。
countriesEn: The first Persian invasion of Greece, which began in 492 BC, was the first time the Achaemenid Empire moved against Europe with the full weight of its imperial army, and it pitted that empire against a loose league of Greek poleis. The Persian side was not a single national army but an imperial levy system organised around a Persian and Median core: Darius I, who styled himself King of Kings, ruled through satraps appointed at Sardis and Persepolis, and the provinces were assessed for men, ships and supplies. The expedition was commanded by the king in person and split into a main body and detached columns; the main army, pressed by Thessalian cavalry at the defile of Anassus, still advanced south in close order with its archers in line, and a separate detached force was sent towards the Danube to threaten the northern flank. The heart of the army was the composite-bow infantry of the Assyrian, Median and Persian tradition: archers carried their own quivers, vast numbers of hired slingers and light spearmen were posted on the wings, and there were Persian heavy infantry and chariot troops. The right wing and the forward line were made up of mixed contingents of Ionians, Lydians, Carians, Phrygians, Sacae, Saramatians and Egyptians, with chariots handled by Persian nobles and Sacae, and a camel corps alongside. The fleet was pieced together from Phoenicians, Cypriots, Cilicians, Egyptians and the Ionians who remained loyal to Persia, and carried heavy rams and siege towers for the attack on Eretria and for covering the landings. On the Greek side the organisation was by city-state: the Athenians elected a board of ten strategoi, each with one vote, and the Council of Five Hundred, the Areopagus and the Assembly decided whether to take the field; Eretria was a small city on the island of Euboea; Plataea was tiny but had been the first ally to stand up; the Thessalian confederacy had scored a success with its cavalry at Anassus; and Sparta and Athens, though they had marched to the aid of Thessaly, turned back on a rumour that the Persians meant to strike the Peloponnese, so the Thessalians were left with a lasting grievance against the coalition. In sum, Persia brought a host on the order of a million men and several hundred ships against a fragmented and loosely coordinated league of city-states, and that imbalance in scale and in kind is the fundamental fact of this war.
people: 大流士一世是這場戰爭的策動者，他在《貝希斯敦銘文》自述的目的包括懲罰希臘城邦、擴張王國，並打算在攻破雅典後縱火焚市；他派遣大將達提斯與阿塔弗爾涅斯率艦隊先行，自身在多瑙河方向另有安排。達提斯是出身羅得斯島的腓尼基裔將領，阿塔弗爾涅斯是波斯王族，兩人先後在埃雷特里亞與馬拉松指揮登陸部隊。希臘方面最關鍵的人物是米太亞德：他在雅典公民大會上力主立刻接戰，理由是趁波斯人尚未完全登岸時以全軍出擊，否則各城邦的援兵無以為繼，雅典將孤立無援；他的同父異母兄弟希庇亞斯隨波斯軍在場，並曾向波斯人指點如何攻入阿提卡，這段家族與波斯之間的不快記憶後來一再被提起。執政官卡利馬庫斯以抽籤方式擔任，握有否決權，最後投下決定性一票贊成立刻出戰；海軍將領忒修斯在阿提刻海峽的追擊中另立功勞。普拉提亞的援軍在開戰前才及時趕到，占據左翼。消息傳回雅典後，希庇亞德之子斐迪庇德斯以約四十公里的奔跑把捷報送入城，後世視之為體育與國民精神的象徵。此役之後，阿里斯泰德與地米斯托克利斯先後在政治上抬頭：前者被後世歸功於推動陶片放逐法，以防再出現一位獨夫；後者則主張擴充艦隊，其主張在此後十年逐步實現。希羅多德是這場戰役最重要的事後記錄者，他對馬拉松雙方兵力的記載成為後世討論的基礎。
peopleEn: Darius I was the man who set the war in motion; in the Behistun Inscription he set down among the purposes of his reign the chastisement of the Greek cities and the extension of the kingdom, and he meant to burn the market of Athens once the city had fallen. He sent the generals Datis and Artaphernes ahead with the fleet. Datis was a commander of Phoenician descent from Rhodes, while Artaphernes was of the royal house, and the two took charge of the landing force in turn at Eretria and at Marathon. The decisive figure on the Greek side was Miltiades, who argued in the Athenian Assembly that the army must attack at once while the Persians had not yet finished putting their men ashore, for otherwise the contingents of the other cities would never arrive and Athens would stand alone. Miltiades' own half-brother Hippias was with the Persian army and had pointed out to them how to enter Attica, a piece of family history that has never stopped rankling. The polemarch Callimachus, chosen by lot, held the casting vote and finally cast it for immediate engagement, and the naval commander Themistocles won separate distinction in the pursuit off the Attic coast. The Plataean reinforcement reached the field only just before the fighting began and took the left wing. Once the news came back to Athens, Pheidippides, son of Hippias, carried it on foot over roughly forty kilometres, and the run was later turned into a national image of physical and civic vigour. After the battle Aristides and Themistocles both rose in Athenian politics: the former was credited by later tradition with pushing the ostracism, put in force in 487 and 486 BC, as a guard against another man of Miltiades' sort, while the latter pressed for a stronger fleet, a claim that was realised step by step over the following decade. Herodotus is the most important later witness to the campaign, and his figures for Marathon remain the foundation on which all discussion of it rests.
kits: 卡面這件亞述長弓，是公元前七世紀亞述帝國成熟的短型複合反曲弓：全長約一公尺上下，箭矢約六十至七十公分、配銅或鐵製箭鏃，射程雖不及希臘式長弓，但在密集隊形中射速快、箭雨平直，能在數百步內壓制敵方射界。亞述人把它編成了弓兵先行、車兵隨進的戰法：步兵以籃形柳條盾掩蔽全身，蹲姿齊射後再整隊前推，車上的射手居高臨下覆蓋陣線側翼。亞述帝國公元前六一二年滅亡後，這套射術與車兵戰法傳給米底，再傳給波斯；到馬拉松，卡面上的弓已是兩百年後的波斯改型（常見說法稱之為波斯—米底複合弓），但基本形制、編制與射擊原則與亞述弓兵同源，希臘人正是面對這一套亞述式的弓陣，才取得馬拉松的勝利。波斯軍的完整裝備還包括木柄斧、鐵矛與阿奇納克斯短匕，護身用鱗甲或皮甲短裙，頭戴有頰飾的高冠盔；弓兵自攜箭袋，容量約數十支，另有大量投石手與輕裝矛兵配置於兩翼。希臘方面，雅典重裝步兵以青銅科林斯式頭盔、青銅蒙面圓盾與亞麻布背心的重裝方陣列陣，矛短而盾密；銀幣夜鷹由勞里翁銀礦供給，成為這場戰爭的財政基礎，其中一部分撥給雅典作軍費。攻城方面，埃雷特里亞的圍城由撞角與登城塔完成，海上由三列槳戰船與平底運載船執行；糧秣由各行省按比例供給，主力大軍沿途設營，渡海靠赫勒斯滂海峽的浮橋與船隊。
kitsEn: The bow on the card is the short composite recurve bow matured by the Assyrian Empire in the seventh century BC: roughly a metre in length, it fired arrows of some sixty to seventy centimetres tipped with bronze or iron. Its range was shorter than that of a Greek longbow, but it shot fast and its volleys fell flat and dense, enough to dominate the enemy's field of fire within several hundred paces. The Assyrians organised it into a system in which archers led and chariots followed: infantry crouched behind wicker shields of the kind the Greeks called the spara, which covered the whole body, loosed volleys in unison and then advanced in line, while archers in the chariots covered the flanks from above. After the fall of Assyria in 612 BC this archery and chariot system passed to the Medes and thence to the Persians. At Marathon the bow on the card is the later Persian adaptation, two centuries on, but its basic form, its place in the order of battle and its shooting doctrine all descend from the Assyrian archers, and it was precisely this Assyrian-style bow formation that the Greeks broke at Marathon. The rest of the Persian equipment included hafted axes, iron spears and the short kinakes dagger, with scale or leather skirts for protection and crested helmets with cheek pieces; archers carried their own quivers with several dozen arrows each, and large numbers of slingers and light spearmen were posted on the wings. On the Greek side the Athenian heavy infantry fought in the phalanx with bronze Corinthian helmets, the bronze-faced round shield, and linen cuirasses, short spears and dense shields. The silver owls of Athens, struck from the silver of Laurion, were the financial base of the war, and part of that silver was earmarked for the army. On the siege side Eretria was reduced by rams and towers, while at sea a fleet of triremes and shallow transports carried the landing parties. Food and fodder were furnished by the provinces in fixed shares, the main army pitched camp as it marched, and the crossing of the Hellespont was made by the fleet and by a pontoon bridge.
tactics: 波斯方的戰術藍圖是三段式：先以艦隊與海路切斷希臘城邦之間的聯繫，再以埃雷特里亞為跳板登陸阿提卡，最後攻取雅典。大流士的命令是先把海軍與大軍集中在優布亞島南端的埃雷特里亞；該城被圍攻、封鎖而後陷落，城破之後波斯人把居民擄走，雅典人則因為事先得到情報而撤到島北的卡爾基斯，避開了這場集體擄掠。海軍隨後依計畫轉向阿提卡，若無阻礙便可直取雅典；但波斯統帥在靠岸與行軍之間反覆斟酌，登陸點最終選在馬拉松的沼澤平原，那裡雖距雅典約四十公里，右翼卻有沼地與一道山脊可倚，適合重裝步兵列陣。登陸延誤反而給了雅典時間：米太亞德率領的一萬重裝步兵連夜行軍抵達馬拉松，與後到的普拉提亞一千人會合，列陣於正面，把隨大軍而來的希臘裔雇傭兵（主要是伊奧尼亞與卡里亞人）放在兩翼，波斯貴族與近衛居中。開戰時波斯人先以箭雨與投石手覆蓋希臘陣線，再以步兵與車兵向前推進，陣形中央強、兩翼弱的排法與希臘方相似，結果希臘重裝兵在兩翼得手，中間的精銳波斯兵卻被拉開；兩翼希臘兵隨即向中央包抄，形成雙面包圍，波斯陣線由此崩解。追擊中希臘兵一度衝到波斯船邊，海軍未及完全接應登陸的隊伍，波斯軍損失七艘船，殘餘兵力退入海船，隨艦隊返回亞細亞。以往希臘作戰多在城牆與海灣之間進行，此役則把陣地選在平原上，雙方都沒有退路，這種一決勝負的取向成為希臘城邦日後打法的起點。
tacticsEn: The Persian plan had three stages: first cut the links between the Greek cities by sea, then use Eretria as a bridgehead for a landing in Attica, and finally take Athens. Darius's order concentrated the fleet and the army on Eretria at the southern tip of Euboea. The city was besieged, blockaded and then stormed; its inhabitants were carried off, while the Athenians, warned in advance, withdrew north to Chalcis and escaped the sort of collective abduction the Eretrians suffered. The fleet then turned to Attica and, if nothing obstructed it, could have gone straight to Athens. Instead the commanders hesitated over the choice of landing, and the beach was finally taken at Marathon, a marshy plain about forty kilometres from Athens whose right side offered a hill and marsh on which a phalanx of heavy infantry could stand. The delay in landing handed the Athenians the initiative: Miltiades led ten thousand heavy infantry by night march to Marathon, joined there by a thousand Plataeans who had come up at the last moment, and arrayed them face to the enemy, with the hired Greek and Carian light troops of the Persian force on the wings and the Persian nobles and picked troops in the centre. When the battle opened, the Persians covered the Greek line with arrows and slings, then pressed forward with infantry and chariots, and the deployment, strong in the centre and weak on the wings, mirrored the Greek array. The result was that the Greek heavy troops won on both wings while the Persian centre was drawn apart; the two Greek wings then wheeled inward and enveloped the centre, and the Persian line collapsed. In the pursuit the Greeks reached the Persian ships, where the fleet had not yet managed to receive the whole landing force, and seven ships were lost. The survivors re-embarked and the fleet returned to Asia. Where Greek warfare had formerly been fought between walls and bays, this battle was set in the open plain, where neither side could retreat, and that appetite for a single decisive encounter became the starting point of later Greek practice.
data: 關於兵力數字，唯一的系統來源是希羅多德《歷史》，他明確寫的是波斯人自己報出的數目，因此要當作宣傳口徑看待。希羅多德記公元前四九二年的遠征總兵力為一百萬上下，其中亞洲步兵約七十萬、伊奧尼亞與卡里亞步兵八萬、海軍陸戰隊三萬、騎兵約一萬，另有大量非戰鬥隨行人員。國王在色雷斯的多爾基斯庫營點驗兵力的場面，是這份數字的核心來源。艦隊方面，希羅多德在十年後描述薛西斯遠征時才給出明細：腓尼基人連同塞浦路斯與塞浦利科亞人分擔七百艘，其餘各邦合計約五百艘，伊奧尼亞同盟按傳統義務提供一百二十艘，總數約一千二百艘；公元前四九二年那一支艦隊沒有留下同等詳細的清單，一般認為規模在數百艘以上。公元前四九〇年的馬拉松遠征，兵力和艦隊都少於兩年前，希臘方面的常見估計是波斯步兵約兩萬、騎兵約五千、另有約一萬輕裝散兵，艦隊數百艘。希臘方面投入馬拉松的是雅典一萬名重裝步兵，另有一支規模在數千人的受雇傭輕裝兵與弓箭手屯紮城內，實際參戰人數應遠低於此，另有普拉提亞約一千名重裝步兵。傷亡數字同樣出自希羅多德：波斯軍陣亡約六千四百人，雅典軍陣亡一千九百二十一人，含陣亡的執政官卡利馬庫斯，普拉提亞的陣亡者另葬；這是古典世界保存下來最早一批有明確記錄的戰役傷亡對照。距離方面，馬拉松到雅典約四十至四十三公里，即斐迪庇德斯送信所跑的全程；戰役在公元前四九〇年九月發生，時距公元前四九二年的渡海行動約兩年。
dataEn: The only systematic source for the numbers is Herodotus, whose fifth and sixth books give figures the Persians themselves reported, so they should be read as a public claim rather than a count. Herodotus puts the expedition of 492 BC at about a million men in all, including roughly seven hundred thousand Asian infantry, eighty thousand Ionian and Carian infantry, thirty thousand marines and about ten thousand cavalry, plus a very large train of non-combatants. The review of the army by the king at Doriscus in Thrace is the core source for these figures. On the fleets he gives a detailed list only for the expedition of Xerxes ten years later: the Phoenicians, with the Cypriots and Cilicians, provided seven hundred ships, the other nations about five hundred, and the Ionian League furnished a hundred and twenty by long-standing obligation, for a total of about twelve hundred. The fleet of 492 BC left no list of equal detail, and is generally thought to have numbered several hundred vessels. The expedition to Marathon in 490 BC was smaller in men and in ships than the one two years earlier, and the usual estimates are about twenty thousand Persian infantry, five thousand cavalry and some ten thousand light-armed troops, with a fleet of several hundred ships. On the Greek side, Athens committed ten thousand heavy infantry, with a body of some thousands of hired light troops and archers kept inside the walls, so the number actually engaged was far lower, and Plataea brought about a thousand hoplites. The casualty figures come from the same author: about six thousand four hundred Persian dead and one thousand nine hundred and twenty-one Athenian dead, the latter including the polemarch Callimachus, while the Plataeans buried their own dead apart; these are among the earliest clearly recorded battle casualty counts to survive from the ancient world. As for distances, Marathon lies about forty to forty-three kilometres from Athens, the length of Pheidippides' run, and the battle was fought in September 490 BC, roughly two years after the crossing of the straits in 492.
cause: 直接導火線是伊奧尼亞起義的餘波。公元前四九九至四九四年，米利都為首的伊奧尼亞城邦聯盟起兵反抗波斯統治，雅典與埃雷特里亞曾出兵援助；起義雖在拉代海峽被鎮壓，但薩迪斯在縱火中受損，波斯王宮被燒的事給大流士留下難以磨滅的記錄，這也是後來大流士一世之妻阿托莎在《貝希斯敦銘文》裡要求報復的說法之一。深層原因則是帝國安全的算計：只要愛琴海東岸的城邦仍與雅典往來，希臘人就會不斷把戰火帶到亞細亞的西岸，波斯在安納托利亞的行省就永遠不穩；大流士把這次遠征定義為懲罰性的懲戒戰役，同時以龐大兵力震懾整個希臘世界，讓其他城邦不敢再伸手。希臘方面的接戰理由則直接而急迫：埃雷特里亞陷落後，優布亞島已淪為波斯海軍的基地，雅典若在對方艦隊立足未穩之前不作反擊，整座城邦連同比雷埃夫斯港都會被鎖死；此外波斯軍原本還打算在攻下雅典後焚燒市集，這段打算在希臘方面的記述中留下很深的記憶。
causeEn: The immediate trigger was the aftermath of the Ionian Revolt. Between 499 and 494 BC the Ionian cities led by Miletus rose against Persian rule, and Athens and Eretria had sent ships to help them. The revolt was crushed after the defeat in the straits of Lade, but Sardis had burned during it, and the damage done to the royal palace in the fire was a memory Darius could not put down; it is the kind of grievance that the queen Atossa invokes in the Behistun Inscription when she demands retribution. The deeper cause was a calculation of imperial security: as long as the cities of the eastern Aegean kept ties with Athens, the Greeks would keep carrying war across to the western coast of Asia, and the satrapies of Anatolia would never be quiet. Darius defined this expedition as a punitive and disciplinary campaign, and at the same time meant the mass of his host to frighten the whole Greek world into keeping its hands off. The Greek case for fighting was immediate and urgent: with Eretria fallen, Euboea had become a naval base for Persia, and if Athens did not strike before the fleet was established there, the city would be shut in along with the port of Piraeus. The Persian plan also included burning the market of Athens after the city had fallen, and that intention lingered long in the memory of the Greek accounts.
impact: 馬拉松是波斯帝國第一次在歐洲大陸被希臘軍隊正面擊敗，而且敗得毫無懸念：全場戰鬥從登陸到登艦不過大半日，波斯百萬大軍的戰爭機器因為一處登陸點的選擇而整體停擺。戰略上，雅典沒有被攻陷，焚燒市集的計劃泡湯，海軍基地也沒有取得；戰役雖然沒有消滅遠征軍本身，卻把波斯不可戰勝的形象第一次在歐洲打上裂痕，直接影響其後的戰略節奏：大流士遇刺身亡，兒子薛西斯兩度集兵，公元前四八〇年的第二次入侵規模遠大於這次。更深一層的影響在希臘內部：這場勝利帶來對個人權力的疑慮，公民大會在公元前四八七至四八六年推行的陶片放逐法，被亞里斯泰德一系的政治說法解釋為防止再出現一個米太亞德式的人物；海軍的價值同時被抬高，地米斯托克利斯主張擴充艦隊的意見在此後十年逐步實現，德洛斯聯盟的建立更把雅典推向海權國家。史學上，這場戰役的意義至今仍在爭論：有人視之為希臘城邦制度抵禦專制帝國的樣板，也有人指出它的成果有限，遠征軍並未被消滅、雅典也未反攻波斯本土；正因如此，它既屬保衛戰，也帶有展示戰的味道。
impactEn: Marathon was the first time a Persian army had been beaten in open battle on European soil, and it was beaten without the slightest doubt: the whole action, from the landing to the re-embarkation, lasted less than a day, and the war machine of a host numbering in the millions stopped dead over the choice of one landing place. Strategically, Athens was not taken, the plan to burn the market came to nothing, and no naval base was secured. The battle did not destroy the expedition, but it was the first crack in the image of Persian invincibility in Europe, and it shaped the pace of what followed: Darius was assassinated, his son Xerxes gathered his armies twice, and the second invasion of 480 BC was on a far greater scale. Deeper still was the effect inside Greece. Victory raised the fear of individual power, and the ostracism carried out by the Assembly in 487 and 486 BC was explained by the political tradition around Aristides as a safeguard against another man of Miltiades' sort. The value of the navy was raised at the same time; Themistocles' argument for a bigger fleet was realised step by step over the following decade, and the formation of the Delian League turned Athens into a maritime power. Historians still argue about the significance of the battle: some treat it as a model of the Greek polis standing against a despotic empire, others point out how limited the results were, since the expeditionary army was not destroyed and Athens never counter-attacked Persian territory. That is why it is at once a defensive battle and something of a display.
result: 結果是雙方都沒有得到想要的東西，波斯人輸掉了登陸戰，雅典人輸掉了把戰果轉化為戰略的機會。波斯軍在馬拉松被擊退後當日重新登艦，退往優布亞島，中途曾企圖在雅典人追擊之前襲擊雅典市集，最後只帶走殘餘艦隊與被擄的埃雷特里亞人返回亞細亞；被奪的七艘船與大量落水者留在希臘海岸，埃雷特里亞全城被掠去居民後荒廢。希臘方在馬拉松平原收埋一千九百餘名陣亡者，執政官卡利馬庫斯與三百多名雅典重裝兵家的墳墓列在公墓之外，戰後盟邦代表會議以特殊決議保障陣亡者家屬的撫恤，這段盟邦決策的傳說後來被雅典民主派用來論證自己制度的優越。軍事上最大的遺憾是追擊：第二次阿提刻遠征雖然出動了六十艘三列槳戰船，卻沒有攔截正準備撤往優布亞的波斯艦隊，放棄了把遠征軍整支消滅的機會，雅典人此後很少再主動進攻，戰爭的正面成果因此長期停滯。遠征軍雖然退回本土，波斯對希臘的戰爭並未結束，大流士在公元前四八九年遇刺，薛西斯於公元前四八〇年再度大舉入侵，馬拉松的勝利只是為這場延續十年的戰爭拉開了序幕。
resultEn: The outcome left both sides without what they wanted: the Persians lost the landing battle, and the Athenians lost the chance to turn a tactical victory into a strategic one. After the repulse at Marathon the Persian force re-embarked the same day, fell back to Euboea, made one more attempt to strike at the market of Athens before the Athenians could catch them, and finally returned to Asia with the remnant of the fleet and the deported people of Eretria. The seven captured ships and a large number of men lost in the water were left on the Greek coast, and Eretria was stripped of its inhabitants and left in ruins. The Greeks buried more than nineteen hundred of their dead in the plain of Marathon, the grave of the polemarch Callimachus and of the families of more than three hundred Athenians was placed outside the public cemetery, and the council of the allies afterwards voted special measures for the families of the fallen, a story of collective decision that Athenian democrats later used to argue for the superiority of their own constitution. The great military regret was the failure to pursue: a second expedition into the Attic coast took out sixty triremes, yet did not intercept the Persian fleet on its way to Euboea, and the chance to annihilate the whole expeditionary army was let go. Athens rarely attacked again, and the direct results of the battle stayed at that level for a long time. The expedition returned to Asia, but the Persian war in Greece was not over: Darius was assassinated in 489 BC, Xerxes invaded again in 480 BC, and the victory at Marathon was only the opening of a war that would run for another ten years.
